paper.title_en: Mapping Domain-Wall Bayesian Reconstruction with LISA
paper.abstract_en: We study the Bayesian reconstruction of peaked domain-wall gravitational-wave signals with LISA and construct reconstruction maps over the signal-parameter plane. These maps identify regions where the signal can be probed with minimal posterior uncertainty and parameter degeneracy. Our analysis employs a two-parameter domain-wall spectral template and includes astrophysical foregrounds from Galactic double-white-dwarf binaries and extragalactic compact binaries, together with LISA instrumental noise. Bayesian inference is performed for 64 injections using nested sampling, and the resulting posterior quantities are interpolated with the Clough--Tocher method to generate smooth maps across parameter space. Under the adopted instrumental-noise and foreground assumptions, we find that LISA reconstructs domain-wall signals most effectively for annihilation temperatures $T_*\sim10^3\!-\!10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}$. In this regime, posteriors become tighter and less degenerate, enabling reliable two-parameter reconstruction. The most favorable region corresponds to signals with ${\rm SNR}\gtrsim50$, while signals with ${\rm SNR}\sim10$ remain reconstructable near $T_*\sim10^{5-6}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. This weaker-signal region corresponds approximately to $4\times10^{-12}\lesssimΩ_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak}h^2\lesssim4\times10^{-11}$ and $30\,\mathrm{mHz}\lesssim f_p\lesssim100\,\mathrm{mHz}$. Our results provide a quantitative reconstruction forecast for peaked domain-wall signals in the LISA band and a guide for particle-physics models predicting milli-Hz gravitational-wave spectra.
